summary: Replaced the PulseAudio backend with a pure Windows WASAPI implementation and ported engine.c. (1) New shared WASAPI layer src/audio/wasapi_device.{h,c}. The header is GLib-only, with no windows.h, so the routing area can include it from portable files. It provides: per-thread COM MTA helpers; MMCSS "Pro Audio"; a refcounted process-wide realtime helper (timeBeginPeriod(1), opt-out of power throttling/EcoQoS including timer-resolution throttling, and a PowerCreateRequest "system required" request); an Audiosrv state query; IMMDeviceEnumerator enumeration giving stable endpoint ids, UTF-8 friendly names, mix channels/rate and default/communications flags; lookup of unplugged endpoints; an exclusive-mode max-rate probe; an IMMNotificationClient written in C (correct QI/AddRef/Release) that forwards changes to registered callbacks under a GRWLock and is safe against late callbacks after unregister; event-driven shared-mode streams for render, capture, endpoint loopback ("<id>.monitor") and process loopback. The process loopback uses ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync with manually declared activation structs and a C completion handler that also answers IAgileObject. Streams request float32 stereo at the given rate with AUTOCONVERTPCM|SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY|NOPERSIST and fall back to the mix format with in-layer channel and sample conversion. Capture mapping is deterministic: mono duplicated, more than two channels downmixed. Other stream features: IAudioClock positions, underrun/discontinuity/silent counters, DEVICE_INVALIDATED classification (REOPEN while the endpoint is still active, else LOST), a Turkish error table, per-bus session names with a ducking opt-out, an audio-session enumeration helper (pid, start time, exe, resolved display name, endpoint), and test/diagnostic hooks (fault injection, simulated Audiosrv outage, COM object counters, COM self-test). (2) src/audio/wasapi_backend.c implements the full renamed engine contract radios_audio_backend_*. It runs a manager thread (connection, hotplug with 250 ms trailing debounce, atomic list publish with cancel/restart, 1 s/2 s/5 s reconnect, Audiosrv watch), three event-driven MMCSS bus threads (MAIN/CUE/MONITOR) and an MMCSS microphone/loopback thread. Pulse semantics are kept: tag/played_tag/consumed_frames/spans/meters come from the device clock only, in-place flush via Stop+Reset with the refill rule, a 100 ms flush handshake, a 5 s route retry, and reconnect that never auto-starts playback. Explicit ids never fall back; Pulse names from Linux preferences give "bulunamadı". It also adds silent bounded reopen on invalidation and stall detection. The device code sits behind a provider seam (RadioSAudioProviderOps + radios_audio_backend_new_with_provider), so a later null/CI provider plugs into the same core. The server locator becomes radios_audio_server_resolve(): NULL, then $RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER, then "wasapi"; anything else is an unsupported locator with a Turkish error. (3) engine.c: backend renames; both time-zone sites now use radios_time_zone_new (D3); the two ~732 KB RadioSAudioRunItem stack arrays and the two 134 KB control-thread snapshots moved to the heap; MMCSS on radios-render; realtime acquire/release around realtime engines; runner path checks use radios_path_is_absolute. No Pulse remnants are left in my files. (4) tests/test_wasapi_backend.c has 16 cases. 7 always run (COM objects, watch lifecycle, plus the Linux hotplug/atomic-publish contract ported onto a deterministic fake provider, service loss/reconnect, locator) and 9 need hardware (RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1). All were actually run on this laptop. The -60 dBFS 1 kHz tone (at most 1 s per case) on the default output came back through the loopback at exactly 0.001000 amplitude at both 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz, with 0 dropout frames, in 5 consecutive final runs. The machine now also has a Pioneer DDJ-FLX10 as the default device, with rekordbox running.
api:
include/radios/audio.h (public):
- RadioSAudioEngine *radios_audio_engine_new(gboolean realtime, const gchar *server)  [parameter renamed from pulse_server; doc updated]
- const gchar *radios_audio_backend_display_name(void)  -> "Windows ses (WASAPI)" (for preferences.c:517)
- guint radios_audio_backend_max_sample_rate(void)  -> highest exclusive-mode or mix rate of any active output, 0 if unknown; cached and never does COM on the calling thread; if no engine has scanned yet, the first call waits at most 1 s (for preferences.c hardware_max_rate)
- Struct layouts unchanged; only the comment "actual ready device stream".

src/audio/audio_internal.h (internal):
- RadioSAudioRing + radios_audio_ring_read/write unchanged (still defined in engine.c).
- typedef struct RadioSAudioBackend RadioSAudioBackend; RadioSAudioBackendSnapshot = the old RadioSPulseSnapshot fields plus guint64 underruns[3], gap_frames[3] (silence inserted while playing = dropouts) and device_scans.
- radios_audio_backend_new(RadioSAudioRing *outputs[3], RadioSAudioRing *capture, const gchar *server); _apply(b, prefs); _configure_output(b, rate, frames); _refresh(b); _flush(b); _flush_buses(b, mask); _snapshot(b, out); _reconnect(b); _free(b); const gchar *radios_audio_backend_label(b). Signatures and semantics are identical to radios_pulse_backend_*.
- gboolean radios_audio_server_resolve(const gchar *server, gchar error[256]): server, then $RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER, then "wasapi"; TRUE for wasapi; FALSE with "Bu ses sunucusu adresi Windows'ta desteklenmiyor: %s". Patchbay and channel_input must use the same rule.
- Provider seam: RadioSAudioIoStatus, RadioSAudioHotplugKind/Sink, RadioSAudioStreamInfo, RadioSAudioProviderOps {label, create, destroy, thread_enter, thread_leave, connect, disconnect, service_running, scan, max_rate, open, wait, padding, write, read, position, start, stop, reset, underruns, last_error, close}; RadioSAudioBackend *radios_audio_backend_new_with_provider(outputs, capture, ops, config). The wake object passed to ops->wait is a RadioSWasapiWaker.

src/audio/wasapi_device.h (shared WASAPI layer, GLib types only, fully documented in the header):
- Threads: radios_wasapi_thread_enter(error)/thread_leave(); radios_wasapi_audio_priority_begin()/end(cookie) (MMCSS "Pro Audio"); radios_wasapi_realtime_acquire()/release(); radios_wasapi_service_running(); radios_wasapi_copy_text(dst, size, text) (UTF-8-safe truncation).
- Endpoints: RadioSWasapiEndpoint {id, name, flow, channels, rate, state, is_default, is_default_communications}; radios_wasapi_enumerator_new/free/list(flow, out, cap, &count, cancelled, data, &cancelled_out, error)/lookup(id, out)/default(flow, id); radios_wasapi_endpoint_max_rate(e, id, &in_use).
- Hotplug: RadioSWasapiChange {kind ADDED/REMOVED/STATE/DEFAULT/PROPERTY, endpoint_id, new_state, flow, role, relevant}; radios_wasapi_watch_new(e, error)/watch_add(w, func, data)->id/watch_remove(w, id) (waits for running callbacks)/watch_free(w).
- Waiting: RadioSWasapiWaker new/signal/free; radios_wasapi_wait(stream, waker, timeout_ms) -> TIMEOUT/WAKER/STREAM/FAILED.
- Streams: RadioSWasapiStreamSpec {kind RENDER|CAPTURE|LOOPBACK|PROCESS_LOOPBACK, endpoint_id ("<id>", "@default", "<render id>.monitor"), process_id, exclude_process_tree, rate, buffer_frames, session_guid[16], session_name, raw, activation_timeout_ms}; radios_wasapi_stream_open(e|NULL, spec, &stream, &info, error) -> OK/LOST/REOPEN/SERVICE_DOWN/FAILED; _padding, _write(stereo|NULL=silence, frames), _read(stereo, cap, &frames, &flags SILENT|DISCONTINUITY), _position (IAudioClock frames at rate), _start, _stop, _reset, _stats {frames, underruns, discontinuities, silent_packets, timestamp_errors}, _error, _hresult, _close. A stream belongs to the thread that opened it.
- radios_wasapi_process_loopback_supported(reason) (cached runtime probe); radios_wasapi_sessions_list(e, include_self, out, cap, &count, error) -> RadioSWasapiSession {pid, start_time FILETIME, exe, name, endpoint_id, active}, one entry per pid, sorted; radios_wasapi_process_start_time(pid, &t).
- Diagnostics/tests: radios_wasapi_debug_inject_fault(INVALIDATED|DEVICE_GONE|SERVICE), radios_wasapi_debug_service_outage(ms), radios_wasapi_debug_counters(&c) {notify_clients, activation_handlers, streams, unreleased_clients, notifications}, radios_wasapi_debug_com_selftest(error), radios_wasapi_debug_watch_emit(w, kind, id).
Device id contract (persisted): IMMDevice::GetId() string; "<render id>.monitor" = loopback; "@default" = eConsole default resolved at open and never followed afterwards; "" = unassigned. Session GUIDs/names per bus: "RadioS MAIN/CUE/MONITOR/mikrofon".
Link: -lole32 -luuid -lavrt -lwinmm -lpropsys -lmmdevapi -lshlwapi -lversion -ladvapi32 (plus FFmpeg swresample through output_resampler.c).
verification: Strict compile (D7 recipe: -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 -DUNICODE -D_UNICODE, MSYS2 UCRT64 gcc 16.2) of src/audio/wasapi_device.c, src/audio/wasapi_backend.c, src/audio/engine.c (against the platform agent's real include/radios/platform.h), src/audio/output_resampler.c and tests/test_wasapi_backend.c: all exit 0 with no warnings, after the final edits.

Early layer probe on hardware: enumerated 2 render and 2 capture endpoints (DDJ-FLX10 at 44.1 kHz is the default, Cirrus Logic at 48 kHz). The -60 dBFS 1 kHz tone was recovered through endpoint loopback, and through process loopback of our own PID at 0.000998. The probe also found that IAudioClient::GetService(IAudioSessionControl) left 1 reference on 3 of 4 clients after close. Switching to IAudioSessionManager::GetAudioSessionControl brought every client to refcount 0; this is now asserted via unreleased_clients == 0 after every test case.

test_wasapi_backend.exe without RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI: 7 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed. Passing cases: COM self-test, watch lifecycle, atomic publish (snapshot max 0.1-5.4 ms), hotplug visible after 262-487 ms with exactly one scan per 50-event burst and no scan for ignored events, 64+64 devices under rescans, service loss and reconnect in about 1 s, unsupported locator and resolver.

test_wasapi_backend.exe with RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1 on this laptop (TZDIR pointed at runtime\python\Lib\tzdata\zoneinfo because core loudness_policy.c is not ported yet): 16/16 passed in 5 consecutive runs of the final binary. MAIN tone at 48000/2400 and at 44100/1024 (the resampler path) came back at 1 kHz amplitude 0.001000 with neighbouring bins at 0.000000, 0 underruns and 0 gap frames. played_tag stayed monotonic and below the written tag; consumed frames tracked real time; an in-place flush kept MAIN ready. Bogus GUID and Linux Pulse names gave the 'bulunamadı' errors. Silent reopen after injected invalidation raised no engine-visible error. Injected device loss gave 'çıkarıldı' and the route retry restored MAIN in 10-17 ms. A simulated Audiosrv outage disconnected and cleared the lists, then reconnected. Max rate reported 192000 Hz. The engine-level realtime case consumed about 48 frames/ms on MAIN, a bogus MAIN device gave 'bulunamadı', and MAIN recovered after restore. Process loopback measured 0.000895-0.000998. Sessions listed this process with the correct start time. The microphone (DDJ-FLX10 input) was opened for 0.33 s; only a peak value was kept and nothing was stored.

Earlier runs failed on harness problems, not backend bugs; each was diagnosed with scratch instrumentation. A 44.1 kHz coherence drop was traced, with a tap on the written signal, to the normal-priority producer thread being starved (mid-stream low-water pads coincided with every phase jump). With an MMCSS producer, as the engine now uses, 6/6 diagnostic runs had zero pads and zero jumps. A missed loss report came from the harness calling reconnect before snapshot; the engine does the reverse. One 22 ms snapshot appeared under desktop load; that led to the devices-lock split, and it has not recurred in 7 later runs.

Engine linking for the test used scratch-only stubs for decoder.c/output.c/transition.c (other areas' files do not compile on Windows yet), plus the real dsp, tempo, transition_preset, loudness_policy, rhythm, loudness and platform*.c objects. The stubs live in the scratch dir only, not in the project.
Syntax-checked other includers of audio_internal.h (output.c, patchbay.c, tests/test_output.c): their errors come only from their own unported POSIX/Pulse code; none come from the header.
industrial_fixes: Per-reopen COM leak avoided: a session control taken via IAudioClient::GetService pins the IAudioClient (and its endpoint buffer) after release. It is now obtained from IAudioSessionManager by session GUID; refcount 0 at close is verified by the test.

Resampled (44.1 kHz) output path no longer zero-fills the resampler source when a second pass finds the ring short (the Pulse code did). That inserted a gap and a phase jump in the middle of a song while the device still had audio queued. It now produces only from real audio, and silence is used only below the low-water mark.

Silence padding is limited to the low-water mark (2 device periods) instead of filling the whole latency target with zeros when the ring is momentarily short. This avoids audible silence between real audio during start/ramp phases while keeping played-position accounting exact.

Device-list publication and snapshot copies (132 KB) moved under a separate lock that the MMCSS bus threads never take. This removes a priority-inversion window where a preempted normal-priority thread could stall the audio threads.
Removed a 512 KB memset under the backend lock on every stream open/flush (playback_tags clearing was unnecessary by construction).

Stream invalidation with the endpoint still present (format change, sleep/resume, driver restart) is a silent bounded reopen (3 attempts per 2 s, queued ring PCM kept) instead of an on-air loss that paused every deck. After that it becomes a loss with a Turkish reason. Added a 2 s stall watchdog for streams that stop signalling.

Explicit device ids never fall back to another device. Unknown ids (including PulseAudio names in preferences migrated from Linux) give 'bulunamadı' plus a route retry instead of an error or a silent substitution. The '@default' device is resolved at open time and never moved later; an automatic move to a newly plugged headset would be an on-air incident.

All Pulse English operator errors (e.g. 'Requested sink is unavailable...', 'Playback resampler queue overflow') replaced with Turkish what-happened/what-to-do texts, truncated only at UTF-8 boundaries.

engine.c: the two ~732 KB RadioSAudioRunItem stack arrays (runner_append, player_runner_configure) moved to the heap; every return path frees them. A stack overflow risk existed with the 2 MiB default Windows stack, deeper with nested planner calls.
engine.c: the control thread's two 134 KB backend snapshots moved from the stack to the heap.

engine.c: both time-zone sites use radios_time_zone_new(). With GLib's g_time_zone_new_identifier, any IANA loudness-policy zone failed apply_preferences on Windows, so no device preferences were ever applied. Also added NULL-safe unref of loudness_zone.
engine.c: runner media and jingle path checks use radios_path_is_absolute instead of g_path_is_absolute. The old check accepted '\foo', '/foo' and device paths on Windows.

engine.c render thread and the backend's bus/mic threads run as MMCSS 'Pro Audio'. While a realtime engine exists, timer resolution is 1 ms, the power-throttling/EcoQoS opt-out includes the minimized-window timer-resolution throttling, and an idle-sleep power request is held (visible as 'RadioS yayın ses motoru çalışıyor' in powercfg /requests). Without these, 3 ms polls stretched to 15.6 ms and minimised or idle machines could drop audio or sleep on air.
Every bus/mic session opts out of Windows communications ducking and uses NOPERSIST volume, so Teams or Zoom can never duck MAIN and RadioS never leaves persisted per-app volume state behind.
New dropout diagnostics per bus (gap_frames, underruns) in the backend snapshot, for operators and the future soak test.
requests_for_other_areas: Integrator (CMakeLists.txt): in radios_audio, replace src/audio/pulse_backend.c with src/audio/wasapi_backend.c and src/audio/wasapi_device.c. Drop pkg_check_modules(PULSE) and PkgConfig::PULSE. Link radios_audio with ole32 uuid avrt winmm propsys mmdevapi shlwapi version advapi32. Remove the test_pulse_hotplug target. Add test_wasapi_backend (tests/test_wasapi_backend.c linked with radios_audio + radios_core). Without the env var it runs 7 no-hardware cases; also register a 'hardware'-labelled variant with ENVIRONMENT RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1. wasapi_device.c defines COBJMACROS/WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN itself and is the only TU that includes initguid.h.

Core area (src/core/loudness_policy.c:31-36): radios_audio_loudness_policy_validate() still tests $TZDIR or /usr/share/zoneinfo/<id> as a file and calls g_time_zone_new_identifier. On Windows that rejects even the default 'UTC', so every radios_audio_engine_apply_preferences() fails with 'Invalid loudness normalization policy'. Use radios_time_zone_identifier_exists()/radios_time_zone_new() from platform.h. My engine test needed TZDIR pointed at runtime\python\Lib\tzdata\zoneinfo as a workaround.

UI area (src/ui/preferences.c): replace hardware_max_rate() (/proc/asound) with radios_audio_backend_max_sample_rate(), and the 'PulseAudio / PipeWire' label (line 517) with radios_audio_backend_display_name(). In src/ui/audio_ui.c:1711, reword 'Ses sunucusu bağlı değil...' for Windows (e.g. 'Windows ses hizmetine bağlı değil; hizmet açılınca kendiliğinden bağlanır.').

Routing area (next phase, patchbay.c/channel_input.c): build on src/audio/wasapi_device.h. Use radios_wasapi_stream_open with PROCESS_LOOPBACK, LOOPBACK ('<id>.monitor') or CAPTURE; radios_wasapi_sessions_list for the application list; radios_wasapi_process_start_time for identity; radios_wasapi_process_loopback_supported for the version probe; radios_wasapi_watch_* for hotplug; RadioSWasapiWaker plus radios_wasapi_wait in the I/O threads; radios_wasapi_enumerator_lookup for friendly names of unplugged endpoints. Use radios_audio_server_resolve() for the locator (same env var RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER) and the same device-id contract. Never call the layer from the GTK STA thread except the [any] functions.

Test-infrastructure area: implement a deterministic null/virtual provider ('null:' locator) on the RadioSAudioProviderOps seam (radios_audio_backend_new_with_provider exists; radios_audio_server_resolve currently reports 'null:' as unsupported). The realtime cases of test_audio, test_audio_recovery, test_audio_soak, test_preferences_output, run_audio_ui.py and test_channel_input capture need it on CI machines without sound hardware. A provider's wait() must return TRUE at least once per period for a started render stream, or the core treats the stream as stalled after 2 s.

Decoder/output/transition owners (src/audio/decoder.c, output.c, transition.c): engine.c links against them, and they do not compile on Windows yet (O_CLOEXEC, fsync, openat...). I linked my test with scratch-only stubs until they are ported.

Docs: docs/08-ses-motoru.md (pulse_backend.c, libpulse/pactl/parec wording) and docs/10-playlist-ve-otomasyon.md:209 still name src/audio/pulse_backend.c; point them to wasapi_backend.c and wasapi_device.c.

Tools: tools/radios_hardware_check.py uses pactl. It needs a Windows inventory, e.g. a RadioS.exe --audio-inventory-json mode built on radios_wasapi_enumerator_list (ids, names, channels, mix rate, defaults).
open_issues: No null/CI provider yet. Until the test-infrastructure work above lands, the 'null:' locator yields connected=FALSE with the Turkish 'unsupported' error, so Pulse-era realtime tests that need virtual sinks cannot run on Windows yet.
Engine-level test cases were verified with scratch link stubs for decoder.c/output.c/transition.c. The real CMake link of test_wasapi_backend against radios_audio is pending integration.

Physical unplug/replug and real default-device changes were not exercised (they would disrupt the user's live audio). They were covered by fault injection (invalidated / device gone / service outage), the fake-provider hotplug cases and the notification self-test. An operator checklist for real unplug and replug is recommended.

Choosing 44.1 kHz output on a 48 kHz device means double conversion (RadioS 48k->44.1k plus Windows SRC back to the mix rate). This is kept deliberately for contract fidelity; true low-latency output via IAudioClient3 and RAW mode is not enabled (RAW is supported in the layer but buses keep Windows' default processing).

At small buffers (e.g. 44100 Hz/1024) the device-side margin is about 23 ms. Gap-free output depends on the engine render thread keeping up; it is now MMCSS, and gap_frames/underruns are exposed in the backend snapshot but not yet shown in the UI.

A few English operator strings remain in engine.c ('Deck has no output route', 'Automation source start window has expired', 'Verified automation media ended before its declared cue span', decoder fallback texts). They are not Windows-specific and were left unchanged.
The test opened the default microphone (DDJ-FLX10 input) for 0.33 s and played a -60 dBFS 1 kHz tone for at most 1 s per case on the default output; no audio was persisted.
